newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Walhold jumps after Bidvest, Investec buy.
newsitem.headline: Walhold jumps after Bidvest, Investec buy.

text.p: Tuesday's announcement that South African retailer Pepkor Ltd had sold ailing stationer Waltons to investment group Bidvest Ltd and Investec Bank Ltd boosted shares in the firms early on Wednesday.
By 0740 GMT Waltons parent Waltons Consolidated Investment Holdings Ltd (Walhold) was up nearly four percent or 35 cents to 920 cents. Waltons was steady at 930 cents but bid at 934 cents.

Bidvest gained 25 cents to 35.30 rand. Pepkor, although untraded was being bid at its overnight closing price of 23.80 rand and offered at 25.50. Investec remained steady near its year high of 178 rand.
The deal, announced late on Tuesday, involves investment firm Bidvest buying with immediate effect the entire business and trademarks of Waltons Stationary Co Ltd for 966 million rand.
In a separate deal Pepkor sold its holdings in Waltons and its parent Walhold for 408 million rand to Investec and an institutional investor.
Dealers said the deal had been welcomed by the market, confirming heated earlier speculation of a Bidvest purchase of Waltons.
"The shares have not moved too much as a lot of it (deal) has already been factored into the prices," one dealer said.
He added however, that in the medium and long-term the purchase was viewed as especially positive for Bidvest.

Bidvest, which will pay for the Walton's operations by issuing 28 million shares at 34.50 rand each, will also pay Pepkor an extra 39 million rand for a restraint of trade agreement prohibiting Pepkor from entering into competition with business currently undertaken by Waltons for two years.
Bidvest chairman Brian Joffe said that the group would remain comfortably cash flush even after the Waltons acquisition, adding that this meant it would remain acquisition-hungry.
Investec paid 9.68 rand per share for the 15 percent Pepkor held directly in Waltons and 9.35 rand per share for the 34.9 percent held in Walhold.

Business Day newspaper reported on Wednesday that a Bidvest spokesman said that he expected the shares paid for Waltons would be distributed to Waltons shareholders. This would leave Investec with a structure which the merchant bank said it "could do something with later down the line", the paper said.
Pepkor's remaining 18.2 percent interest in Walhold was taken up by an unnamed institutional investor.
In the year to February 28, Waltons' headline earnings slumped to 50.0 cents a share from 69.4 cents before. A restructure programme had been put in place to remedy this.
